big: A salaried client has EPF. She also opened a PPF and an NPS. Three building blocks, each with its own rules for interest, lock-ins and exit. Mixing them up leads to mistakes.

lines: How do EPF, PPF and NPS differ?

EPF: for salaried employees, employee and employer contributions earn a notified interest rate, with conditions on withdrawal. PPF: a 15-year government-backed scheme with a yearly deposit limit, and the rate reset by the government each quarter. NPS: a market-linked pension account with equity, corporate bond and government bond choices. Tier I is locked until retirement age, with partial withdrawals in specific cases. At exit, part must buy an annuity. Rules have been updated several times, so check the latest.
